???+ remember "Before you start, remember"

    ??? question "What do we call one small, automatic check with a definite pass or fail answer?"

        A test. It either passes or fails, with nothing in between.

        Introduced in [0. The workbench](stage-0-workbench.md).

    ??? question "Which international standard do Vortex's `f32` and `f64` follow?"

        IEEE 754, the standard for floating-point arithmetic.

        Introduced in [Learn: 8. Runtime and numerical rules](../../language-tour/06-runtime-and-numerical-rules.md). Specification: [4. Types and values](../../specification/types-and-values.md#44-floating-point-values).

    ??? question "In `for index in 0..4 { ... }`, what is `index`, and where can it be used?"

        The loop variable. It is visible only inside the loop's body.

        Introduced in [Learn: 6. Statements](../../language-tour/09-statements.md). Specification: [6. Statements and control flow](../../specification/statements.md#68-for-loops).

    ??? question "What do we call the number of dimensions of an array, such as 2 for `[f32; 2, 3]`?"

        Its rank. An indexing expression must give one index for each dimension.

        Introduced in [Learn: 5. Expressions](../../language-tour/08-expressions.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../../specification/arrays.md#75-rank-and-shape).

    ??? question "Which v0.1 type holds a fixed number of values of one type, with sizes known at compile time, such as `[f32; 4]`?"

        A fixed-size array. Its element type and every dimension are part of its type.

        Introduced in [Learn: 4. Variables and types](../../language-tour/04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../../specification/arrays.md#71-array-types).
